title: Canonical System Package
description: The MASTER SCHEMA for the complete canonical system package. This is the single source of truth for an entire project — every phase of the kernel reads from and writes to this package. It unifies intent, success model, architecture candidates, selection rationale, synthesis, audit results, routing state, evolution history, and final outputs into one coherent object.

metadata.description: Package-level metadata for identification, versioning, and lifecycle tracking.

package_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this package instance. Format: UUID v4.

project_id.description: The project identifier, matching the intent metadata.project_id.

version.description: Semantic version of this package. Incremented on each successful audit pass.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of initial package creation.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent modification to any field in this package.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the package.

kernel_version.description: Version of the universal systems kernel that produced this package.

intent.description: The compiled intent object produced by Phase 1.

success_model.description: The success model produced by Phase 2, defining how the architecture will be evaluated.

candidates.description: Architecture candidates generated by Phase 3. Typically 2-4 candidates with distinct structural biases.

selection.description: The result of Phase 4 (Candidate Selection). Records which candidate was chosen, whether it was hybridized from multiple candidates, and the rationale.

chosen_candidate_id.description: The candidate_id of the selected candidate. If hybridized, this is the ID of the newly created hybrid.

hybridized_from.description: If the selected architecture is a hybrid of multiple candidates, list the source candidate IDs here. Empty array if a single candidate was selected as-is.

rationale.description: Detailed explanation of why this candidate (or hybrid) was selected. Must reference the success model dimensions and tradeoff priorities.

confidence.description: Confidence level in the selection (0.0 = no confidence, 1.0 = fully confident). Low confidence may trigger additional candidate generation.

synthesis.description: The fully synthesized architecture produced by Phase 5. This is the detailed, implementation-ready architecture derived from the selected candidate.

subsystems.description: Fully detailed subsystem definitions, expanded from the candidate's subsystem sketches.

interfaces.description: Fully specified interface contracts between subsystems.

flows.description: Detailed runtime flows with error handling, timeouts, and latency budgets.

dependencies.description: External dependencies — libraries, services, cloud resources, third-party APIs.

control_points.description: Points in the system where behavior can be dynamically controlled — feature flags, rate limiters, circuit breakers, config-driven routing.

feedback_loops.description: Feedback mechanisms — monitoring-to-alerting, auto-scaling triggers, health-check-driven routing, canary analysis.

failure_containment.description: Failure containment boundaries — blast radius definitions, bulkheads, fallback chains.

evolution_paths.description: Anticipated future evolution paths — how the system can grow, split, or transform as requirements change.

audit.description: Audit state from Phase 6. Contains the current audit vector, history of previous vectors, and aggregate counts.

current_vector.description: The most recent audit vector. Null if audit has not yet been performed.

previous_vectors.description: History of all previous audit vectors, ordered chronologically. The most recent vector is NOT included here (it is in current_vector).

pass_count.description: Number of times the architecture has passed audit. Typically 0 or 1.

reroute_count.description: Number of times the pipeline has been rerouted due to audit failure.

routing_state.description: Current state of the kernel pipeline routing engine.

reroute_target.description: If status is 'rerouting' or 'overdrive', this is the phase the pipeline is looping back to. Empty otherwise.

mode.description: The runtime mode governing pipeline behavior. 'standard' is normal operation. 'search_heavy' increases candidate exploration. 'conservative' reduces risk tolerance. 'overdrive' applies maximum remediation effort.

evolution.description: The evolution ledger — a chronological record of every mutation applied during reroute/overdrive cycles.

outputs.description: Final deliverable paths and references produced by Phase 7 (Delivery).

blueprint_path.description: File path to the generated architecture blueprint document.

manifest_path.description: File path to the generated build manifest.

package_summary.description: A human-readable summary of what was built, key decisions made, and confidence level.

handoff.description: Handoff configuration for delivering the package to downstream consumers.

downstream_targets.description: List of downstream consumers that will receive this package (OS teams, CI pipelines, external systems).

adapter.description: The adapter used for delivery format translation, if any. Empty if delivering natively.

delivery_method.description: How the package is delivered to downstream targets.

notes.description: Free-form notes for the downstream consumers — known issues, caveats, implementation priorities.

synthesis_subsystem.description: A fully detailed subsystem in the synthesized architecture.

purpose.description: What this subsystem is responsible for.

responsibilities.description: Granular list of responsibilities owned by this subsystem.

deployment_unit.description: How this subsystem is deployed (container, lambda, static, etc.).

data_ownership.description: Data entities owned by this subsystem.

contract_format.description: Format of the interface contract (openapi, protobuf, asyncapi, graphql, etc.).

authentication.description: Authentication mechanism used on this interface.

sla.description: Service level agreement for this interface (latency, availability, etc.).

control_point.description: A dynamic control point in the system.

location.description: Subsystem or interface where this control point lives.

signal_source.description: Where the signal originates (metric, log, health check, etc.).

action.description: What action is taken when the signal triggers.

trigger_condition.description: The condition that activates this feedback loop.

containment_strategy.description: How failures within this boundary are contained.

trigger.description: What would trigger this evolution (scale threshold, new requirement, etc.).
